findings.where: Phone first screen: the cut-out head between the nav links and the heading
findings.fault: The head is squeezed into the gap between the nav row and the heading. The hair nearly touches the nav links, and the cut-off neck and suit stop hard on the heading's first line. Mark reads as a floating head jammed between two blocks of text, not as a photograph with room around it. Proximity also merges the nav, the face and the heading into one cramped stack.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer opening the site on a phone would see Mark's face crowded against the menu and headline. It looks careless at the exact moment the page asks for trust in a personal advisor. The founder judges the first screen first and wants Mark seen with real weight.

findings.where: Hero, desktop and phone: the 'Placeholder: Mark's photo…' caption
findings.fault: The photo caption is set far from the photo. On desktop it sits at the bottom left under the email action, while the photo fills the right half. On phone it sits below the action, a full screen of text below the head it describes. By proximity it reads as a note on the action or the text block, not on the photograph.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile, who needs to see at a glance which image is a stand-in. Any visitor would also take the note as being about the email box beside it.

findings.where: Header vs footer and the sections below the hero (desktop)
findings.fault: The nav, name and hero text hang on a 58 px left edge. Everything below, including the footer's logo, name and address, hangs on a 170 px edge. The page has two left edges, so the footer lockup does not line up under the header lockup it repeats (continuity breaks).
findings.who_objects: A reader scrolling to the footer for the address finds the logo and name in a different place from the top of the page. It is a small looseness that a careful advisor's site should not have.

findings.where: Article specimen: the PDF row ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', 'Lecture · 23 April 2026'), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The title and date in the PDF row are indented about 4 px from the article's text column, so they sit just off the left edge that every paragraph, the image, the subhead and the rules share.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the founder, who will take this row as the pattern for the whole PDF list. A near-miss alignment looks like a mistake, not a choice, and it will repeat on every row.

findings.where: Palette specimen, phone: the text-pair table's Ratio column
findings.fault: At 390 px the first ratio breaks as '11.66 :' with the '1' on the next line. The swatch labels ('warm / white on slate') also wrap around the Aa chip, so the rows look ragged and the ratio does not read as one value.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Angélique checking the palette on a phone would misread the split ratio, and the table looks broken there.

findings.where: Type pair specimen, desktop: the Newsreader and Public Sans descriptions
findings.fault: The two columns do not share a top line. Public Sans's description starts about 30 px higher than Newsreader's, because each follows its own specimen's height. The pair looks offset, not set side by side for comparison.
findings.who_objects: The founder comparing the two faces side by side. The skew draws the eye to the misalignment rather than the type.
